description:
Plan which vehicle delivers which orders, in what order, and when each
vehicle leaves the depot, minimising customer waiting time.

Built for live dispatch through a busy shift, where orders keep arriving
and each driver goes out many times. Call it again whenever new orders
come in or a driver returns, with every order not yet sent out. Dispatch
only each vehicle's first run: later runs are a look-ahead the next call
revises.

Every order is assigned, so the vehicles' combined capacity (times
max_deliveries_per_vehicle) must cover all orders. Returns per-vehicle
stop lists with ETAs and each order's wait versus its target, plus
headline KPIs. The plan is a recommendation: nothing is stored or sent
to drivers.

The plan minimises how long customers wait, with an extra cost per minute
an order is late. Far orders get a little more time than their wait
target (distance_grace_minutes in the result). Set freshness to the
user's kind of goods (hot meals, iced coffee, ...) to keep sensitive
orders' rides short. The defaults suit same-day food delivery.

Freshness.description:
Goods class for how fast an order loses quality on the road. Resolved
by optimise() into a degrade start and weight relative to
factor_wait_excess - see FRESHNESS_TERMS and LESSONS_LEARNED.md
("Freshness classes").

address.description: Street address, geocoded server-side when lat/lon are omitted
address.title: Address

freshness.description: How fast the order loses quality on the road: robust (not modelled), hot (hot meals), cold (iced coffee, cold drinks), crispy (fries, delicate food) or frozen. Omit to use plan_deliveries' freshness.

priority.description: Send this order out as soon as possible
priority.title: Priority

ready_at.description: When the order is ready to leave the depot. Omit to mean now.
ready_at.title: Ready At

received_at.description: When the customer placed the order. Omit to mean now.
received_at.title: Received At

wait_target_minutes.description: Promised wait, from received_at to arrival at the customer
wait_target_minutes.title: Wait Target Minutes

Place.description: A location given either as a street address or as coordinates.

address.description: Street address, geocoded server-side when lat/lon are omitted
address.title: Address

Place.title: Place

available_at.description: When the vehicle is back at the depot and free for a new route. Omit if it is available now.
available_at.title: Available At

capacity.description: How many orders the vehicle can carry at once
capacity.title: Capacity

id.description: Your reference for the vehicle or driver
id.title: Id

depot.description: Where the vehicles start from. Omit only if your API key is bound to a depot, in which case the server supplies it.

factor_wait.description: Cost per minute of every order's wait, from received_at to arrival (default 1). Only its ratio to factor_wait_excess matters; leave the default unless the user asks for something specific.
factor_wait.title: Factor Wait

factor_wait_excess.description: Lateness weight: extra cost per minute an order is late, beyond its wait_target_minutes plus distance grace (default 10), so 40 minutes late costs far more than 5. Values from 1 to 100 give similar plans: the default keeps the late tail down without raising the average wait. Change it only if the user asks to trade one for the other.
factor_wait_excess.title: Factor Wait Excess

freshness.description: Freshness class for orders that don't give their own, usually the shop's kind of goods: hot (hot meals), cold (iced coffee, cold drinks), crispy (fries, delicate food), frozen, or robust (not modelled, the default). Sensitive orders get shorter rides at a cost of about 0.5-1 minute average wait per protected class.

max_deliveries_per_vehicle.description: How many consecutive delivery runs to plan per vehicle. Only the first run of each vehicle needs dispatching now: plan again when a vehicle returns.
max_deliveries_per_vehicle.title: Max Deliveries Per Vehicle

optimization_seconds.description: Solver time budget in seconds; more can give slightly better plans. Below 5 the plan is returned with a warning, as priority orders may not be sent out first.
optimization_seconds.title: Optimization Seconds
